cases.title: With natural order switched on, the Pit Schedule lists P1, P1A, P1B, P2 ... P9, P9A, P10, P10A, then C1, SPS2, SPS10, every row in its place, even though the pits were placed in a scrambled order
cases.plan_item: UX-SCHED-06 Pit Schedule natural order, the whole chain with the refinement on (daily card D21 assertions 2 and 4; switch linking.pitScheduleNaturalOrder ON, OFF in Tim's file); strengthens N34 after cx_cr25
cases.expected: With the switch on, six pits placed with PIT and their numbers typed in New Pit, in this placing order: P10A at 152000,-80000, SPS10 at 154000,-80000, P9A at 156000,-80000, P1B at 158000,-80000, SPS2 at 160000,-80000, P1A at 162000,-80000 (cover 19.000, three Esc each). 'Pit placed successfully.' appears six times. The Pit Schedule then lists exactly P1, P1A, P1B, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6, P7, P9, P9A, P10, P10A, C1, SPS2, SPS10 in that order, with no other pit row between any two of them.
cases.why_not_unit: The order shown depends on the live schedule window reading the real pits, with the real Settings switch, after live placements with typed numbers.
not_automated: Tim's own file has this switch OFF; this proves the switch-ON setting only. The twin N40_BROKEN (switch off) shows the order Max gets today.
The LPD, OG and CP groups are N33 (switch off). A newly placed P8 taking its number's place is N29. Names such as LPD1 or OG2, and saved row order or schedule filters, are not driven.
SPS2 and SPS10 are typed names on ordinary pits; the SPS pit TYPE is not tested.
